summary: Downtown west of Great George is red-brick commercial rows on Queen, Grafton and Richmond around the Confederation Centre, a handful of mid-century office blocks (the beige Dominion Building with the library, brown-brick federal and provincial blocks), the brick CN-era Rodd hotel with its white portico on Kent, and the Kirk's tall stone spire; beyond Pownal it turns into painted Victorian clapboard houses, inns and churches, ending in the grand houses at Victoria Park (yellow Second Empire Beaconsfield, white colonnaded Government House). Current events: the Confed Centre's $65M wing finishing fall 2026, the Rodd's six-year rebuild, the DJM Building's $100M renovation, a transformer fire closing the Jean Canfield Building (March 2026) and The Banks apartments going up on the Haviland waterfront lot.

buildings.name: Rodd Charlottetown hotel, Kent Street at Pownal
buildings.facts: Built 1930-31 by Canadian National Railway (one of six CN hotels, four survive); five storeys, 115 rooms; the Queen stayed in 1964. A $10M+ exterior and room renovation began 2023-24 in eight stages over about six years, hotel open throughout: crumbling brick from freeze-thaw and rusting steel beams, the first two truckloads of replacement brick were 'too orange', new windows, insulation, sprinklers, groundwork for geothermal. Heat and power cost about $1,200 a day (2024). The Rodd chain is a real business: needs a stand-in.
buildings.look: Georgian Revival railway hotel, red-orange brick with cream cast-stone trim: a stone belt course over the ground floor, cream panels/swags under the top cornice, a grey-cream stone cornice, an oval bull's-eye window in a carved cream cartouche high on the centre. Five storeys plus a recessed attic storey; flat roof with copper-green urn finials on the corners of the parapet and a brick chimney stack behind. Main front on Kent Street (south): a white one-storey portico of paired Ionic/Tuscan columns (six columns) over the entrance, with the hotel's name on a black board along the frieze in gold letters. A lower one-storey brick wing with a green (sedum) roof steps down beside the portico on the west. White-framed double-hung windows in a regular grid. Car park and lawn on the east side (toward the fire station).

sign.note: proposed stand-in for Rodd Hotels; alternative 'The Rodent' is too mean

buildings.name: Charlottetown Fire Department, Station No. 1 (Kent Street)
buildings.facts: The city's main fire station and headquarters on Kent Street beside the Rodd; all staff firefighters work from Station 1. A third (West Royalty) fire hall: land bought 2017 for $870,000 near Route 2 and Sherwood Road, design started 2019, put on hold 2023, $6M in the 2026 budget but the mayor says it needs about $12M over two years; the 2026 budget had no money for new full-time firefighters, and the union objected. In Feb 2022 the department told Discover Charlottetown its plan for overhead lights strung across Kent Street east of Great George didn't meet fire code.
buildings.look: 1970s-80s station in orange-buff brick with a rounded brick corner pier at the entrance; a white fascia band over the glazed entrance with the department crest and 'FIRE DEPARTMENT' in red letters; flat roof with brown metal hoods/mansard-like fascia panels and solar panels on the roof (drone photo). Apparatus bay doors (guess: three or four red-framed overhead doors with glass rows) facing Kent Street or the side lot.

buildings.name: Dominion Building (Charlottetown Library Learning Centre), Queen Street
buildings.facts: Former federal building/post office across Queen Street from the Confederation Centre. The public library moved into its ground floor (just over 30,000 sq ft) after 57 years in the Confed Centre; opened 18 July 2022, cost close to $16M, delayed by COVID and supply chains. Upper floors are offices. The library's new front on Queen Street has a café, terrace and outdoor performance pads; a second-floor outdoor terrace.
buildings.look: Seven-storey mid-century office block clad in pale beige limestone-look panels; windows grouped in pairs of white-framed casements in a regular grid; flat roof with a penthouse. 'DOMINION' in tall black capitals running vertically down the Queen Street corner pier, 'BUILDING' small under it (and a tenant name at the top corner). Ground floor on Queen Street: the library entrance pavilion, a flat black steel canopy on thin black columns over a glass wall, with steps, ramps and steel railings down to a brick-paver plaza; a big dark grey monolith sign on a concrete plinth: 'Charlottetown Library Learning Centre' in white with a book logo. Interior: white columns, white shelving, yellow chairs visible through the glass.

buildings.name: The Guild (arts centre), Queen Street at Richmond
buildings.facts: Community arts centre in a 1950s former bank building on Queen Street facing the Confederation Centre: small theatre, a downstairs gallery, rented offices. Ownership passed to the non-profit Ars Longa in 2018. Lost more than $337,000 in three years; Charlottetown council gave $25,000 emergency funding (Dec 2023) as it faced 'imminent collapse'; a Friends of The Guild group formed (Jan 2024); board said in Nov 2024 it had 'turned the corner' by renting the space out on a sliding scale instead of producing its own shows.
buildings.look: Three/four-storey front: a full-height glass curtain wall in dark blue-tinted glass with white mullions, framed by polished black granite and grey granite panels; a giant pink letter 'G' painted on the glass with 'THE GUILD' in white under it; a black LED marquee sign with red scrolling text over a white-framed glass entrance. Faces Queen Street (east, across to the Confederation Centre, whose sandstone shows reflected in the glass). Next to it the brick commercial row with arched upper windows continues down the street.

buildings.name: Jean Canfield Building (federal offices), 191 Great George Street
buildings.facts: Five-storey federal office building, opened 2009-10, $54M, LEED Gold, designed to use 60% less energy than an average office, big rooftop solar array (and a 2011 story about new heaters taking the shine off its green rating). Service Canada and Veterans Affairs offices; VAC's temporary national HQ while the Daniel J. MacDonald Building is renovated; passport printing being added (2026). 12 March 2026: a transformer caught fire outside, cut the main power, building on generator, Service Canada and VAC closed for over a week. The name is a real person's: sign should read 'Government of Canada' / 'Federal Building'.

A low white federal sign on posts at the walk: red flag, 'Jean Canfield Building / Immeuble Jean-Canfield / 191 Great George Street', 'Canada' wordmark. buildings.name: Daniel J. MacDonald Building (Veterans Affairs Canada HQ), 161 Grafton Street
buildings.facts: Veterans Affairs Canada's national headquarters. Staff moved out in 2020-21; EllisDon won the $98M contract (design NORR), work started March 2023 replacing mechanical, electrical and safety systems, target spring 2026, cost about $100M; a 2025-26 CBC video says it's on the home stretch. VAC staff resisted Ottawa's return-to-office order because the building was still closed. The name is a real person's: sign as 'Veterans Affairs Canada'.

'Canada' wordmark and flag on the roof parapet over the Grafton Street corner. Low federal sign on the lawn: 'Veterans Affairs Canada / Daniel J. MacDonald Building' (blue band, white letters). Blue construction hoarding along Grafton during the renovation.

buildings.name: Beaconsfield Historic House, Kent Street at West Street
buildings.facts: Built 1877 for shipbuilder and merchant James Peake, designed by William Critchlow Harris; run by the P.E.I. Museum and Heritage Foundation, the province's flagship historic site; open for tours, lectures, concerts. Restoration of windows, flooring and siding around 2017-19. Stands at the entrance to Victoria Park; walking tours of The Bog start here.
buildings.look: Second Empire house: golden-yellow clapboard with white corner boards and trim, two storeys under a grey slate mansard roof (patterned slates, dormers), a square belvedere/cupola on top with its own little mansard and iron cresting, tall red brick chimneys; a wide one-storey veranda with white posts and fretwork across the front and side. Formal flower beds and lawn in front.

buildings.name: St. Peter's Cathedral (Anglican) and All Souls' Chapel, Rochford Square
buildings.facts: Anglican cathedral founded 1869, almost entirely brick with little stone trim; All Souls' Chapel (1888, William Critchlow Harris, built by the Lowe Brothers, paintings by Robert Harris) is attached on its west side, a National Historic Site since 1990, built of rough Island sandstone. The Queen worshipped here in 1973. Faces Rochford Square, the green on the site of The Bog, Charlottetown's 19th-century Black neighbourhood.
buildings.look: Cathedral: dark red brick Gothic church, steep dark slate roof, pointed lancet windows, buttresses; (guess) a modest belfry/bellcote rather than a tall spire. All Souls' Chapel: small, very steep gabled chapel in rough red-brown Island sandstone with a big pointed window in the gable end and a red door, set lower and attached to the cathedral. A black sign board on two black posts with gold lettering and the diocesan crest: 'St. Peter's Cathedral / Anglican / All Souls' Chapel'.

buildings.name: Kirk of St. James (Presbyterian), 35 Fitzroy Street
buildings.facts: Cornerstone laid 7 June 1877, dedicated 20 October 1878, Gothic Revival by David Stirling (Halifax) with W.C. Harris; replaced the 1831 kirk. Built of Wallace, Nova Scotia freestone with red Island sandstone doorway facings, buttresses and window surrounds. Tower walls 20 inches thick; the spire reaches about 130 ft (40 m): a tall octagonal spire with gabled lucarnes at the base of each side. Famous for the 1853 'phantom bell ringers' ghost story (Canada Post stamp, 2016) and lobster suppers.
buildings.look: Grey-buff freestone Gothic church, steep dark slate roof, pointed windows with red sandstone dressings, buttresses; a square stone tower with a very tall, slender dark octagonal stone/slate spire with small gabled lucarnes round its base, topped by a cross/finial. The spire is the tallest point on the downtown west skyline (visible behind the Rodd in the 2024 drone photo).

Was the Officers' Club (men only), became the Haviland Club in 1997, women admitted 1999; hosts New Year's levees; said to be haunted by three or four spirits; rentable for events.

buildings.name: Government House (Fanningbank), Victoria Park
buildings.facts: Official residence of the Lieutenant Governor, completed 1834 on Fanning's 1789 estate; part of the farm became Victoria Park in 1873 (more added 1905). In 2023 the Lieutenant Governor banned group photo shoots on the grounds after 'extremely disturbing' behaviour (people yelling at her when she intervened); tours of the grounds stay open. Not in the area's named list: find its OSM way in Victoria Park.
buildings.look: Georgian/Palladian house: white clapboard, two storeys, black/dark green shutters on every window, grey hipped roof with tall chimneys; a giant two-storey colonnade of white round columns on the front and a long colonnaded veranda; looks south over lawns and gardens to the harbour. A blue sign with gold letters 'PRIVATE RESIDENCE / RÉSIDENCE PRIVÉE' on a post by the door.

neighbourhoods.name: Downtown west core (Queen, Pownal, Grafton, Kent, Fitzroy between Great George and Rochford)
neighbourhoods.where: Water Street north to Euston, Great George west to Rochford
neighbourhoods.look: Mixed 19th-century core: rows of two/three-storey red-brick commercial buildings with arched upper windows and cornices along Queen, Grafton and Richmond (Victoria Row's 1884-rebuilt brick block), between mid-rise 1960s-80s office blocks (Dominion Building beige stone, DJM brown brick, government blocks) and big surface lots and parkades. Side streets (Pownal, Fitzroy, Rochford) are two/two-and-a-half-storey Victorian clapboard houses, many converted to offices, inns and apartments, painted white, cream, grey, pale blue, sage and heritage reds, with white trim and dark grey/black asphalt-shingle gabled roofs.

neighbourhoods.name: Victoria Park edge / west end (Kent, Grafton, West Street, Pond Street)
neighbourhoods.where: Rochford west to West Street and the park
neighbourhoods.look: The grandest houses in town: large Victorian and Second Empire houses (Beaconsfield, Number One Grafton, Eden Hall, inns), deep lawns, big elms and maples; painted clapboard in yellow, cream, white, sage and grey with white trim; mansard and steep gabled roofs; a few 1970s brick apartment blocks (Park West Lodge) near the park.

neighbourhoods.name: Waterfront west (Water, Haviland, Sydney, Pownal wharf)
neighbourhoods.where: south of Richmond/Water from Great George west to the armoury
neighbourhoods.look: Open land and parking by the harbour boardwalk; the culinary institute (low beige), the armoury (brick), 1990s-2000s condos and apartments (Paoli's Wharf, Renaissance Place eight-storey brown brick), the Haviland Club's white Italianate house, and the new seven-storey Banks apartments under construction on the Haviland lot.

neighbourhoods.name: Rochford Square / The Bog
neighbourhoods.where: Rochford, Kent, Fitzroy, Pownal around St. Peter's
neighbourhoods.look: A green square with mature trees framed by St. Peter's Cathedral and All Souls' Chapel (red brick and sandstone) and the provincial office blocks (Shaw, Jones, Sullivan): 1960s-80s four/six-storey institutional buildings. This was The Bog, the 19th-century Black neighbourhood; the province has committed to a permanent marker (consultations 2026).

neighbourhoods.look: Office and hotel blocks (Quality Inn, Jean Canfield, Atlantic Technology Centre, Homburg tower) among two-storey clapboard houses; Euston Street is the old line developers say the city won't let them build dense housing south of (one apartment south of Euston for every 27 units north of it).

current_events.what: Confederation Centre's $65M renovation of the old library wing (work since Oct 2024, $47M federal share) lowers the floor to Richmond Street level for a Victoria Row entrance; arts academy, 'Canadian Leadership Institute', 'Arts Innovation Hub'; due fall 2026, on time and budget per the CEO. Victoria Row was fenced off from Jan 2025 with no notice to shops ('gut punch'), fully reopened for patios June 2026.

Rodd Charlottetown's six-year, eight-stage, $10M+ renovation (from 2023): 'They built it within one year and it's going to take us six to put it back together'; the replacement brick was 'too orange'; $1,200 a day in heat and power.
Daniel J. MacDonald Building (VAC HQ): $98M contract, about $100M, staff out since 2020-21, finishing 2026; meanwhile Ottawa ordered staff back to offices that were closed for renovation.

Jean Canfield Building, LEED Gold green flagship: a transformer fire outside on 12 March 2026 cut power and closed Service Canada and Veterans Affairs for over a week; Islanders sent to Montague or a website.
West-end fire hall: land bought 2017 ($870,000), design 2019, paused 2023, $6M budgeted 2026 for a $12M job; no new full-time firefighters in the 2026 budget.
The Guild: lost $337,000 in three years, $25,000 emergency city grant (Dec 2023), 'turned the corner' (Nov 2024) by renting itself out.

199 Grafton (Polyclinic lot): six-storey 84 units approved 2021, stalled over the city changing an affordable-housing tax incentive; eight storeys/158 units withdrawn 2023 because zoning allows four; later the 158-unit 'Port House' near approval (2024).
current_events.where: Polyclinic lot, Grafton Street (just east of my area)

current_events.what: Great George at Kent: eight-storey, 85-unit apartments with shops proposed (June 2024) to replace 149-151 Great George (florist, beside Dow's on Confederation Court Mall); planning staff's only worry was traffic.

231 Richmond St. (500 Lot Area): province's housing corporation left the house vacant from 2017, a neighbour's IRAC appeal over demolition (2023), $1.4M for three affordable units under way Aug 2025 after two and a half years; the deputy mayor was 'frustrated' at the staff time.
Government House banned group photo shoots (2023) after visitors yelled at the Lieutenant Governor.
Sir John A. Macdonald bench statue removed overnight (1 June 2021), boxed at Public Works since; 'no plans'.
Guardian building, 165 Prince St.: sold 2019, plan for two more floors of student housing ('Prince Hall') stalled by a $6,000-a-unit parking fee ($360,000), on hold indefinitely (2021).
current_events.where: 165 Prince Street (east of Great George; for downtown_east)
